extracted.intended_audience: prospective EMBO Long-Term Fellowship applicants (postdoctoral researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for applying to the EMBO Long-Term Fellowship programme, including eligibility, documentation, mobility rules, application process, selection criteria, and benefits. Targeted at postdoctoral researchers preparing an online application to EMBO.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD degree or equivalent at the start of the fellowship, but not necessarily at the time the application is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who already hold a PhD are eligible if they obtained their PhD during the two years prior to the date the application is complete. Exceptions are made for prolonged career breaks (parental leave, mandatory military/civil service) and possibly extraordinary personal circumstances (severe illness) — Fellowship Office must be contacted prior to claiming an exception. Candidates with an M.D. may be eligible if they hold a PhD (MD-PhD) or have appropriate research experience comparable to a PhD; contact Fellowship office prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have at least one first (or joint first) author primary research paper accepted for publication or published in an international peer reviewed journal at the time the application is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO will not consider papers that are submitted or in preparation, review articles, patent applications, abstracts of presentations, or publication updates after application. Preprints (arXiv, BioRxiv) are considered, but a first-author publication in an international peer-reviewed journal is still a requirement. Do NOT indicate journal impact factor (EMBO follows DORA). Publication updates after application are not allowed without re-opening the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must involve a change of country; EMBO Long-Term Fellowships are intended to promote international exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International labs such as EMBL are extra-territorial so movement (e.g., university in Germany to EMBL Heidelberg) is permitted. Special rules apply depending on destination: (a) to work in an EMBC Member State — applicants of any nationality or PhD country can apply provided there is international mobility; (b) to work in an EMBC Associate Member State or co-operation territory — applicants must move from, be nationals of, and have performed their PhD in an EMBC Member State, Associate Member State, or co-operation territory; (c) to work in a Non-EMBC Member State — applicants must move from an EMBC Member State, be nationals of an EMBC Member State and have performed their PhD in an EMBC Member State (maximum 30% of fellowships awarded in this category). Movement within the same country is eligible if applicant has been working for a maximum of six months in that country during the previous 18 months counting back from application completion. Candidates already at the host lab are eligible only if they have been there for a maximum of six months at the time the application is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility exclusions / not eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific situations that render applicants ineligible based on mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not eligible: applicants wishing to work in the country where they officially obtained their PhD or where they developed their PhD studies; applicants wishing to work again with their PhD supervisor (no matter location). Applicants who worked in more than one country during PhD should contact Fellowship Office to determine eligibility. Applicants wishing to return to a laboratory where they have already worked for more than six months (in one or several visits) are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposals must be within EMBO’s scientific scope (subject areas listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO subject areas include cell cycle, cell & tissue architecture, cellular metabolism, chromatin & transcription, development/differentiation/death, evolution & ecology, genome stability & dynamics, genomic & computational biology, immunology, membranes & transport, microbiology/virology/pathogens, molecular medicine, neuroscience, plant biology, proteins & biochemistry, RNA, signal transduction, structural biology & biophysics, systems biology. More detail at EMBO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of applications per round
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may only submit one application, for one project, at one host laboratory at each round of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-application policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-application is permitted only once, irrespective of change of project or host lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates can re-apply for the next round while a decision is pending on their first application but should re-apply only if they will not be eligible after the decision on the first one is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial research / applied projects policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to work in an industrial research laboratory with the intention to develop new commercial products or procedures will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications to work in research centres for basic research that are endowed by for-profit organizations are eligible. Projects aiming to develop an application or device based on biological knowledge are not necessarily excluded, but there must be a fundamental biology question behind the project. Development of technologies that enable biological discovery (e.g., microscopy, PCR) will also be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application language and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be written in English and no special formatting is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and tables cannot be included in the application. Applications are submitted via the EMBO online system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and cutoff rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are accepted throughout the year but must meet cutoff dates to enter selection rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete applications received before the second Friday of February 14:00 CET enter Spring Selection Round (results early June). Complete applications received before the second Friday of August 14:00 CEST enter Autumn Selection Round (results early December). Applications completed after 14:00 CE(S)T on deadline day enter the next round; NO EXCEPTIONS. The online system may be closed after deadlines for maintenance; candidates must consider potential downtimes. Registration alone is not sufficient; an application is only complete once all required information is submitted AND the candidate confirms completion. The confirmation date (CE(S)T) is the reference date for eligibility and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documentation required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications require supporting documentation: two reference letters and the acceptance letter from the receiving institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the reference letters must be from the PhD supervisor and none may come from referees in the receiving institute. Applications and supporting documentation are only accepted via the online system. No application can be completed without these documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission changes and publication updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to applications after confirmation are limited; publication updates after completion are not allowed without re-opening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only changes in address or email after submission are permitted without re-opening. All other changes, including publication updates, require the office to re-open the application; re-opening causes a change in submission date to the new completion date which may cause ineligibility. Publication updates after application are not allowed unless application is re-opened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary selection criterion: scientific excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary selection criterion applied by all EMBO committees is scientific excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship Committee seeks the best and most promising young researchers; scientific excellence underpins all evaluation stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant scientific achievements (evaluation aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment includes scientific contributions and CV, and performance of the applicant based on reference letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are considered in the committee's decision alongside project and host lab suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project proposal evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Project proposals are evaluated for quality, novelty and biological significance, and coherent and logical presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that continue exploring a topic similar to the PhD project usually receive lower priority for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host laboratory evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment considers suitability of the host laboratory for the proposed research and training, and the scientific achievements of the host laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications to work with host laboratories with which the candidate has collaborated in the past or to develop a project on a similar topic to the candidate’s PhD work generally receive lower priority for funding. Fellowships are awarded to candidates (not host institutions) but host suitability matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-screening stage procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: First stage (0–5 weeks after cutoff): pre-screening to ensure eligibility and initial assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All complete applications are screened by the EMBO office for eligibility; eligible applications are assessed by three members of the Fellowship Committee using a condensed application form (summary of scientific achievements, publications, summary and biological significance of proposed work, justification for host lab, reference and acceptance letters). Approximately 30% progress to second round. Applicants receive acknowledgement email ~1 week after cutoff and are informed about pre-screen outcome ~5–6 weeks after cutoff. No feedback is provided to applicants rejected at this stage; committee scores applications but cannot include individualized comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview stage procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Second stage (6–14 weeks after cutoff): interview by an expert; seminar required as part of interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interviewer (EMBO Member or Young Investigator) is selected; personal interview preferred but videoconference may be arranged; if interview cannot be arranged, application is sent for written evaluation. Interviews often require travel outside country of residence; candidate arranges interview and travel. Candidates must give a seminar as part of interview. Interview travel expenses are reimbursed by EMBO: choose most economical transport (economy/second class); original receipts and invoices are required (do NOT send scanned copies); subsistence and accommodation covered by flat daily allowance depending on country. A claim form and original receipts must be returned within 4 weeks after interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final selection stage procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Third stage (14–17 weeks after cutoff): five members evaluate each application selected for second stage with interviewer report; committee meets to take final funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary list of awarded applications is published on EMBO website within one week of committee meeting; all applicants officially informed by email within one week of meeting. Successful applicants must start fellowship within specified windows depending on selection round; due to practical limitations fellowships can only start on either the 1st or the 15th of each month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are awarded for a period of 24 months although shorter durations can be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum fellowship duration that can be requested is 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend purpose and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend is solely intended to cover the cost of living in the host country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipend rate depends on country and might be subject to taxation; EMBO does not cover bench fees, overheads, funds for consumables or any other financial benefits to host supervisor or receiving institute. In event of early termination, payments made in advance for periods after termination must be reimbursed to EMBO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent child allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO fellows are entitled to receive a country-specific additional allowance for dependent children under 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See stipend rate sheet for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child care allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: For children under six, fellows can claim support for incurred child-care costs up to €2,500 per fellowship year and per child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount is prorated according to the fraction of the year in which child-care expenses were incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel allowance intended to cover travel costs up to €5,000 for the fellow and his/her family to and from the receiving institute; includes half a month’s stipend to contribute to relocation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant is already at the receiving institute at application completion or has been working at the host lab for more than 6 months at the start of the fellowship, the travel allowance will not be paid. If fellowship is terminated within the first 6 months, entire travel allowance must be returned; if terminated within the 7th–12th month, half must be repaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows whose children are born during their fellowship are entitled to 3 months paid parental leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows who take parental leave are entitled to an extension of their fellowship for an equivalent period; extension must be requested by the host supervisor at the end of the fellowship. Parental leave must begin within 6 months of the birth and fellows must inform the Fellowship Office of intention to take parental leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time work allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Part-time work is possible for child-care reasons at 50% or 75% of full time during the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum fellowship duration (full-time plus part-time) must not exceed 36 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private pension scheme participation and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO offers participation in a private pension scheme; during fellowship EMBO functions as policyholder and deducts fellows’ contributions from stipend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO matches fellows’ contributions up to €100 per month. After fellowship ends the policy is transferred to the fellow. If a fellow voluntarily contributes to another pension scheme, EMBO will also match contributions up to €100 per month paid at the end of each year, provided the scheme is a proper pension scheme (not life insurance/investment account) and transferable to another country, at minimum within Europe.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMBO Fellows' Network and meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the fellowship, fellows are invited to EMBO Fellows' Meeting and (for North America) US Fellows’ Meeting every two years; these events facilitate presentations, experience sharing, collaborations, meeting staff and feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO encourages fellows to follow programme social channels for information and events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory Leadership Course waiver eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-Term Fellows may be granted a limited number of free places (fee waivers) on the EMBO Laboratory Leadership Course for Postdocs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers are granted at the end of the fellowship within 5 years of the award and only if the fellowship had been held for at least 6 months. The waiver covers the course and accommodation; travel costs are not included. Fellows are given priority to courses organized around Fellows’ Meetings to avoid extra travel expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-stipendiary fellowship conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of early termination or non-acceptance of the EMBO Long-Term Fellowship due to funding from another source, long-term fellows can become holders of a non-stipendiary fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-stipendiary Fellows can attend Fellows’ Meetings and, if they hold the fellowship for at least 6 months, the Laboratory Leadership Course free of charge at the end of their fellowship. It is not possible to directly apply for a non-stipendiary fellowship. Applicants who receive another award during the evaluation period and cannot guarantee at least 12 months' take-up of EMBO Fellowship will be excluded from the selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and confirmation date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which candidates confirm that their application is complete (CE(S)T) is the reference date for eligibility and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications completed after the evaluation cutoff time will enter the next evaluation round. Registration for an EMBO online account alone does not enter the evaluation round; the candidate must submit all required information and confirm completion. Re-opening the application to add information will change the submission date to the new completion date.
